core.title: Place every interlocking artifact under the interlocking home
core.given: A plan contains, or is gaining, interlocking artifacts (new or existing); placement is enforced at the CONFIRM phase, so it applies from the moment the interlocking is authored
core.when: The planner authors, edits or moves an interlocking artifact, or brings a plan containing one to CONFIRM
core.then: Every interlocking artifact lives under the interlocking home.
prefer: Place interlocking artifacts under the interlocking home when first authoring them, rather than relocating them at CONFIRM
Ensure each interlocking under the home has an entry in the registry index (registration is a required obligation of the same enforced check; see verification)
avoid: Placing interlocking artifacts alongside other plan-artifact kinds or in other plan folders outside the interlocking home
Leaving an interlocking artifact unregistered in the registry index
core.why: Other interlocking rules (registry mirroring, guards, payloads, route resolution, route-space admission) presuppose the homed and registered interlocking set; an artifact outside the home or registry is invisible to them.
evidence: The confirm-phase placement check over every interlocking artifact in the plan passes
On failure the finding reports the interlocking's id, its path, the expected home and the actual home
verification: Presence check over every interlocking plan artifact in the plan, new and pre-existing: each must lie beneath the expected interlocking home; any path beneath the home, not only directly under it, satisfies placement

Registration is mandatory, not advisory: every interlocking under the home must have an entry in the registry index at the profile's registry path; the realization records a proposed split into its own registration convention, which shares this check and does not remove the obligation here
The check runs at the CONFIRM phase and blocks confirmation; severity 3, strict disposition
On failure the finding reports the interlocking's id, its path, the expected home and the actual home
The check does not cover plan artifacts whose kind is not interlocking

values: plan artifact located under the interlocking home (layout.interlocking_home)
plan artifact that is the interlocking registry index (layout.interlocking_registry)

fires: A plan reaches CONFIRM and contains any interlocking artifact, new or pre-existing
An interlocking artifact is authored, edited, moved or exists somewhere other than under the interlocking home
An interlocking artifact under the interlocking home has no entry in the registry index
doesNotFire: A plan that contains no interlocking artifacts
Plan artifacts whose subject kind is not interlocking (any other plan-artifact kind) when no interlocking is present

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts; the interlocking home and the registry index sit beneath it
Canonical directory under the plan root that is the home of every interlocking artifact; any path beneath it satisfies placement
Registry index file under the plan root in which each interlocking under the home must be registered
The concrete plan-artifact kinds, including the interlocking kind this rule scopes to

proposedKeys.meaning: Directory under the plan root that is the canonical home of interlocking artifacts; any path beneath it satisfies placement
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The layout group covers wagon, feature, commons and single plan-item shapes, but no kind-specific home directory; layout.plan_item is the path of one plan artifact, not the home of a kind

proposedKeys.meaning: Registry index file under the plan root in which every interlocking under the home must be registered
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key names a registry/index file for a plan-artifact kind; urn.* keys describe URN shapes and bindings, not registry files

neutralityNotes: The convention governs plan-artifact placement, so ATDD plan vocabulary (interlocking, plan, planner, the CONFIRM phase) is kept as stack-neutral methodology terminology; the artifact-kind value itself comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The only non-neutralizable content is the concrete home and registry paths, which move to profile keys (proposed layout.interlocking_home and layout.interlocking_registry, no existing vocabulary key fits), and this rule's validator, template and variant ids, which stay bunOnly while core verification names the check generically. The registration half of the Bun statement is enforced, not advisory: core verification requires every homed interlocking to be registered in the registry index, and the realization's splitSuggestion (planner.train.interlocking-registered) records the intent to split it into its own convention without removing the obligation here. The path-based activation trigger is expressed as a role fact scoped strictly to the profiled interlocking home and registry index, while the file_kind fact (needs_new_observer) retains content-based recognition of interlockings anywhere else in the plan.
